recentItems.title: The Life Expectancy Lies That Won't Die
recentItems.description:
In which John explores the question of historical life expectancy, and how sometimes a misleading narrative is corrected by ... a misleading narrative.
If you want to understand historical and present life expectancy in granular detail, I recommend these Our World in Data articles, where I got most of the information in this video:
How Does the Risk of Death Change as We Age? https://ourworldindata.org/how-do-the-risks-of-death-change-as-people-age
Life Expectancy Has Increased at All Ages: https://ourworldindata.org/life-expectancy?insight=life-expectancy-has-increased-at-all-ages#research-writing
It's Not Just about Child Mortality: https://ourworldindata.org/its-not-just-about-child-mortality-life-expectancy-improved-at-all-ages

recentItems.title: Just Trying to Figure Out My Job
recentItems.description:
Just so everyone knows, I have been hearing lots of honest critique and thoughtful perspectives on this. It has not been mostly bad-faith nonsense or "I SUPPORT YOU NO MATTER WHAT"s. Mostly what I'm hearing is, that I need to make things in a way that is honest to how I enjoy creating and that makes it easy for people to know that you're only ever hearing from me. 

The Hank Green AI Policy
1. No portion of any script will be written, edited, or outlined by an LLM.
2. The thesis of a video will always originate with a human. 
3. No image or music in a video will be generated by AI. If something is accidentally included, best efforts will be made to remove it. 

ADDED 7:30PM Mountain time August 7 after reading through comments:
4. LLM outputs will never be trusted as a source.

And this is more of a general policy but:
5. Informational / educational videos will contain links to primary sources in the description.
